The instant petition has been filed praying for a direction to the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners in terms of Section 24(1)(a) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. Shri Sunil Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the petitioners states that the controversy involved in the instant writ petition is identical to the one decided by this Court today in connected Writ-C No.14561 of 2023 (Ram Dhani Patel And 4 Others vs. State of U.P. And 4 Others).

entities.text: Ram Dhani Patel And 4 Others vs. State of U.P. And 4 Others)

1 instant matter be decided in same terms.

entities.text: Umashankar And 11 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Shri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel appearing for the State-respondents also makes the same submission.

4. The operative part of the order in Writ-C No.14561 of 2023 is as follows:
"8. Having regard to the aforesaid admitted fact, we are of the opinion that the provisions of Section 24(1)(a) of the new Act would not be attracted.

It is left open to the petitioners to approach the Special Land Acquisition Officer about the alleged remaining claim and in which event, respondent no.3 will examine the claim and will take appropriate decision in accordance with law within eight weeks from the date, a copy of the instant order alongwith claim is made before him."
5. The instant writ petition, accordingly, also stands disposed of in same terms.

(Kshitij Shailendra, J) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, A.C.J.) Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Ankit.
